newsitem.title: USA: Tosco denies early Penn. refinery restart.
newsitem.headline: Tosco denies early Penn. refinery restart.

text.p: Tosco Corp on Friday afternoon took issue with union claims that it is planning to restart its revamped refinery in Trainer, Penn., by April -- three months ahead of earlier plans.
"The company stands by its earlier statements of a summer startup," said a Tosco official. "It's certainly not expected in April."
Dennis Stephano, president of Local 8-234 of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers union also said Friday the refinery will probably operate with a 180,000 to 190,000 barrel per day (bpd) capacity.
But Tosco, which was not immediately available for comment earlier Friday, countered that the capacity would likely be closer to the company's previously stated goal of 150,000 bpd.
"It could be higher, it's just to early to say," the official said.

Tosco took title to the plant last February, after acquiring the refinery for $25 million, and said it would spend another $50 million to upgrade, cutting the capacity from 180,000 bpd to concentrate on higher value light-end products.
